title: A prayer for words that uproot and plant
source_text: Ἐν τρισὶ τοῖς πρὸ τούτων διεξελθόντες βιβλίοις τὰ πρὸς τὸ Κέλσου σύγγραμμα νοηθέντα ἡμῖν, ἱερὲ Ἀμβρόσιε, τέταρτον πρὸς τὰ ἑξῆς εὐξάμενοι διὰ Χριστοῦ τῷ θεῷ ὑπαγορεύομεν. δοθεῖεν δ᾿ ἡμῖν λόγοι, περὶ ὧν ἐν τῷ Ἱερεμίᾳ γέγραπται, ὡς τοῦ κυρίου πρὸς τὸν προφήτην εἰπόντος· „ἰδοὺ δέδωκα τοὺς λόγους μου εἰς τὸ στόμα σου πῦρ. ἰδοὺ καθέστακά σε σήμερον ἐπὶ ἔθνη καὶ βασιλείας, ἐκριζοῦν καὶ κατασκάπτειν καὶ ἀπολύειν καὶ κατασπᾶν καὶ ἀνοικοδομεῖν καὶ καταφυτεύειν.“ καὶ γὰρ ἡμεῖς νῦν χρῄζομεν λόγων ἐκριζούντων τὰ κατὰ τῆς ἀληθείας ἀπὸ πάσης ψυχῆς. βεβλαμμένης ἀπὸ τοῦ συγγράμματος Κέλσου ἢ τῶν παραπλησίων αὐτῷ νοημάτων. δεόμεθα δὲ καὶ νοημάτων, κατασκαπτόντων πάσης ψευδοδοξίας οἰκοδομὰς καὶ τῆς Κέλσου ἐν τῷ συγγράμματι αὐτοῦ οἰκοδομῆς παραπλήσια τῇ οἰκοδομῇ τῶν εἰπόντων· „δεῦτε οἰκοδομήσωμεν ἑαυτοῖς πόλιν καὶ πύργον, οὗ ἡ κεφαλὴ ἔσται ἕως τοῦ οὐρανοῦ“· ἀλλὰ καὶ χρῄζομεν σοφίας κατασπώσης πάντα τὰ ἐπαιρόμενα „κατὰ τῆς γνώσεως τοῦ θεοῦ“ ὑψώματα καὶ τὸ Κέλσου „ἐπαιρόμενον“ καθ᾿ ἡμῶν τῆς ἀλαζονείας „ὕψωμα.“ εἶτ᾿ ἐπεὶ μὴ χρὴ καταλήγειν ἡμᾶς ἐπὶ τὸ „ἐκριζοῦν καὶ κατασκάπτειν“ τὰ προειρημένα ἀλλ᾿ εἰς μὲν τὴν χώραν τῶν ἐκριζωθέντων „καταφυτεύειν“ φυτείαν τοῦ κατὰ θεὸν γεωργίου, εἰς δὲ τὸν τόπον τῶν κατασκαφέντων οἰκοδομεῖν θεοῦ οἰκοδομὴν καὶ ναὸν δόξης θεοῦ, διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ἡμῖν εὐκτέον ἐστὶ τῷ δεδωκότι κυρίῳ τὰ ἐν τῷ Ἱερεμίᾳ γεγραμμένα, ἵνα καὶ ἡμῖν δῷ λόγους καὶ πρὸς τὸ οἰκοδομεῖν τὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ „καταφυτεύειν“ τὸν πνευματικὸν νόμον καὶ τοὺς ἀνάλογον αὐτῷ προφητικοὺς λόγους. καὶ μάλιστα χρεία ἡμῖν πρὸς τὰ νῦν ἑξῆς τοῖς προειρημένοις τῷ Κέλσῳ λεγόμενα κατασκευάσαι ὅτι καλῶς τὰ περὶ τοῦ Χριστοῦ πεπροφήτευται. ἅμα γὰρ πρὸς ἀμφοτέρους ἱστάμενος ὁ Κέλσος, Ἰουδαίους μὲν ἀρνουμένους γεγονέναι τὴν Χριστοῦ ἐπιδημίαν ἐλπίζοντας δ᾿ αὐτὴν ἔσεσθαι, Χριστιανοὺς δὲ ὁμολογοῦντας τὸν Ἰησοῦν εἶναι τὸν προφητευθέντα Χριστὸν, φησίν·
pass_a_gloss: Having gone through (διεξέρχομαι) in the three books (βιβλίον) before these the things thought out (νοέω) by us against (πρός) the treatise (σύγγραμμα) of Celsus, holy (ἱερός) Ambrose, we dictate (ὑπαγορεύω) a fourth against the things next (τὰ ἑξῆς), having prayed (εὔχομαι) to God through Christ. May words (λόγοι) be given (δίδωμι, optative) to us, about which it is written in Jeremiah, as the Lord (κύριος) said to the prophet: 'Behold, I have given my words into your mouth [as] fire (πῦρ). Behold, I have set (καθίστημι) you today over nations (ἔθνη) and kingdoms (βασιλεῖαι), to root out (ἐκριζόω) and to dig down (κατασκάπτω) and to destroy (ἀπολύω/ἀπόλλυμι) and to pull down (κατασπάω) and to build again (ἀνοικοδομέω) and to plant (καταφυτεύω).' For we too now need (χρῄζω) words rooting out the things against the truth (ἀλήθεια) from every soul (ψυχή) harmed (βλάπτω, perf. pass. ptc., agreeing with ψυχῆς) by the treatise of Celsus or by thoughts (νοήματα) resembling (παραπλήσιος) his. We need (δέομαι) also thoughts digging down the buildings (οἰκοδομαί) of every false opinion (ψευδοδοξία), and the building of Celsus in his treatise, similar to the building of those who said: 'Come, let us build for ourselves a city and a tower, whose head (κεφαλή) will be up to heaven'; but we also need wisdom (σοφία) pulling down all the heights (ὑψώματα) lifted up (ἐπαίρω) 'against the knowledge (γνῶσις) of God', and the 'height' of arrogance (ἀλαζονεία) of Celsus 'lifted up' against us. Then, since we must not end (καταλήγω) at the 'rooting out and digging down' of the things said before, but into the place (χώρα) of the things rooted out 'to plant' a planting (φυτεία) of the farm (γεώργιον) according to God, and into the place (τόπος) of the things dug down to build God's building and a temple (ναός) of God's glory (δόξα), for this reason we too must pray (εὐκτέον) to the Lord who gave the things written in Jeremiah, that he may give us too words both for building the things of Christ and for 'planting' the spiritual (πνευματικός) law (νόμος) and the prophetic words analogous (ἀνάλογον) to it. And most of all there is need (χρεία) for us, against the things said by Celsus next after those said before, to establish (κατασκευάζω) that the things about Christ have been well (καλῶς) prophesied (προφητεύω). For Celsus, standing (ἵσταμαι) at the same time against both, Jews denying (ἀρνέομαι) that the coming (ἐπιδημία) of Christ has happened but hoping (ἐλπίζω) it will be, and Christians confessing (ὁμολογέω) that Jesus is the prophesied Christ, says:

lemmas.note: perf. pass. ptc., agreeing with ψυχῆς

pass_b_english: In the three books before this one, holy Ambrose, we have gone through what occurred to us in reply to Celsus’s treatise. Now, having prayed to God through Christ, we dictate a fourth in reply to what comes next. May we be given words such as those of which it is written in Jeremiah, where the Lord says to the prophet: “Behold, I have put my words into your mouth as fire. Behold, I have set you this day over nations and kingdoms, to root out and to dig down, to destroy and to pull down, to build again and to plant” (Jeremiah 1:9–10; 5:14).

For we too now need words that will root out whatever stands against the truth from every soul that has been harmed by Celsus’s treatise or by thoughts like his. We need thoughts as well that will dig down the buildings of every false opinion, and the building Celsus has put up in his treatise, which is like the building of those who said, “Come, let us build ourselves a city and a tower whose top shall reach to heaven” (Genesis 11:4). And we need wisdom that pulls down every height that is lifted up “against the knowledge of God” (2 Corinthians 10:5), and the “height” of arrogance that Celsus has “lifted up” against us.

Then, since we must not stop at “rooting out and digging down” what we have named, but must “plant” a planting of God’s field in the ground of what has been rooted out, and must build God’s building and a temple of God’s glory in the place of what has been dug down (1 Corinthians 3:9), for this reason we too must pray to the Lord who gave what is written in Jeremiah, that he may give us also words for building up the things of Christ, and for “planting” the spiritual law and the prophetic words that answer to it.

Above all, in answer to what Celsus says next after the passages already treated, we need to establish that what was prophesied about Christ was rightly prophesied. For Celsus stands against both parties at once: against the Jews, who deny that the coming of Christ has taken place but hope that it will, and against the Christians, who confess that Jesus is the Christ who was prophesied. He says:

choices.choice: ‘the answers we conceived to’ → ‘what occurred to us in reply to’ (νοηθέντα, less stiff)
‘a fourth against what follows’ → ‘a fourth in reply to what comes next’ (πρὸς τὰ ἑξῆς)
‘May words be given to us of the kind written of in Jeremiah’ → ‘May we be given words such as those of which it is written in Jeremiah’ (natural order)
Checked Jeremiah 1:9–10 + 5:14 (LXX ‘πῦρ’), Genesis 11:4, 2 Corinthians 10:5, 1 Corinthians 3:9 against the verses; numbering agrees

Copy-text: staged source_4.json section 1 (Koetschau 4.1). Ambrose is Origen’s patron (cf. 3.1); ἱερέ rendered ‘holy’. The Jeremiah quotation joins Jeremiah 1:9 with ‘as fire’ (πῦρ) from Jeremiah 5:14 (LXX: ‘ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ δέδωκα τοὺς λόγους μου εἰς τὸ στόμα σου πῦρ’) and then gives 1:10; Origen’s list adds κατασπᾶν (‘to pull down’), which is not in the LXX of 1:10; translated as he quotes it. LXX and English chapter numbering agree for Jeremiah 1 and 5. Genesis 11:4 matches the LXX wording. 2 Corinthians 10:5 supplies ‘lifted up against the knowledge of God’ and ὕψωμα. ‘God’s field … God’s building’ draws on 1 Corinthians 3:9 (θεοῦ γεώργιον, θεοῦ οἰκοδομή); cited once beside the clause. ‘Temple of God’s glory’ has no single clear source verse; left uncited. ‘The spiritual law’ is a possible echo of Romans 7:14 (‘the law is spiritual’); uncertain, so not cited inline. The staged text has a stray full stop after ψυχῆς; βεβλαμμένης agrees with ψυχῆς, so the sentence is read as one. The chapter ends on φησίν (‘He says:’); Celsus’s words follow at the opening of 4.2.
